y_failures: Says the perpetual motion was 'supposedly mimicking the tides', but p.50 says it was 'not, however, in accordance with that of the sea'. Also lists a Drebbel 'Weather Glass' that Monconys discussed with Kuffler and that Wren later elaborated, cited to p.50; no page supports this, since p.68 is Wren's own hygrometer.
reason: Both quote the bread-oven passage on p.51 accurately, but Y misstates p.50 on the tides and invents a weather-glass item attributed to the Kuffler visit. X's claims, including the brooder from Jaeger p.90 and the register diagram on p.52, are supported by the pages given.
